items.h: Rushing TD in loss
items.s: Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills on Sunday. It was a nightmare of an afternoon for the Ravens offense, which lost both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) during the first half and struggled to move the ball with emergency quarterback Joe Fangano at the helm. Henry's rushing opportunities ultimately suffered as Baltimore's deficit grew, but he managed to punch in a two-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter before matters got out of hand. It's been a relatively rough three-game stretch for Henry following a 102-yard effort on the ground against the Falcons in Week 5, and…

items.h: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 8 loss
items.s: Derrick Henry rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in a 36-10 loss to the Bills. He caught both of his targets for seven yards. Henry found the end zone for the first time since Week 4 against the Titans. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) headed to IR and Tyler Huntley's (toe) status uncertain for Week 9, Henry could be in line for a lot of work against the Jaguars in Week 9.

Derrick Henry Looks to Get Back on Track in Matchup Vs. Bills
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry currently leads the NFL in rushing attempts (147) and ranks sixth in the league in rushing yardage (579). He is tied for third in the NFL in rushing touchdowns (seven). However, Henry is currently averaging a career-low 3.9 yards per carry, and he has rushed for under 60 yards in each of his last two games. He rushed for a season-low 45 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. However, with starting quarterback Lamar Jackson back, things could open up for Henry and Baltimore's ground game in a Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. The Bills have struggled to defend the pass (285.8 passing yards per game allowed), but have been better…

items.h: Week 7 winners and losers: Pollard, Burrow lead the way; Walker III, Purdy struggle
items.s: Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers came up big in Week 7, while Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III all had quiet days.

items.h: Derrick Henry quiet in Week 7 loss
items.s: Derrick Henry rushed for 45 yards on 17 carries in a 35-13 loss to the Bengals. He caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards. The Bengals' defense was able to bottle up Henry all day, leading to his worst performance of the season. The Ravens are hopeful to have Lamar Jackson back in Week 8, which could open up more lanes for Henry against Buffalo.

items.h: Shut down for second straight game
items.s: Henry rushed 17 times for 45 yards and brought in one of two target for four yards in the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. Henry averaged below 3.5 yards per carry for the second consecutive game against a divisional opponent, and Sunday's inefficiency also dropped his season per-carry average under 4.0 (3.9). The bruising back does have seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but none have come within the last three games. Henry will look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 8 road showdown against an improved Bills run defense next Sunday.

items.h: Derrick Henry Held to 45 Yards in Another Week 7 Fantasy Disappointment
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry still carries a substantial workload, but poor efficiency and a lack of scoring chances have produced consecutive fantasy disappointments, including just 45 rushing yards on 17 carries without a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Henry averaged a season-low 2.6 yards per attempt, with his longest run gaining only nine yards. He also caught one of two targets for four yards, finishing with 5.9 PPR fantasy points. Baltimore led 13-0 at halftime but failed to score after the break, with three trips inside Cincinnati's 15-yard line producing only six points. Henry has now rushed for 103 yards on 34 carries without a touchdown…

items.h: Derrick Henry Should Continue Dominant Season in Week 7
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry has been incredible so far this season, and there's no reason to believe that won't continue in Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals. The 32-year-old back is averaging 21.7 rushing attempts per game, 4.1 yards per attempt, and has eight total touchdowns this season. Besides last week's dud of 60 total yards and a fumble against the Cleveland Browns, Henry has averaged about 22 half-PPR fantasy points per game. That ceiling remains, especially if Lamar Jackson is healthy enough to play this week after missing the last two games. Lamar has been dealing with an ankle injury, likely meaning fewer rushing attempts for him, leaving more for Henry.…

items.h: Stymied by Browns in loss
items.s: Henry rushed 17 times for 58 yards and brought in his only target for two yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Henry looked like he was on his way to one of his signature performances when he rattled off 11- and 17-yard gains on Baltimore's opening possession, but the veteran back found running room at a premium for most of the rest of the contest. Henry finished without a touchdown for the second straight game and tallied his lowest rushing yardage total of the campaign, rounding out a disappointing day for the Ravens overall. Henry will aim to bounce back in a Week 7 home divisional matchup against the Bengals next Sunday.

items.h: Week 6 winners and losers: Lawrence, Walker III impress; Robinson, Henry disappoint
items.s: Malik Nabers, Kenneth Walker III and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 6, while Bijan Robinson, Derrick Henry and Kyren Williams underwhelmed.

items.h: Derrick Henry gains 60 scoreless yards in Week 6 loss
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry ran for 58 yards on 17 carries and caught one pass for two yards in the team's 13-10 loss in Cleveland. Henry was held scoreless for the first time this season, ending a five-game streak of rushing/receiving touchdowns that had opened the year. He also lost a fumble in the tight contest. Henry's long-term outlook remains strong, but with Lamar Jackson sidelined, there is a lower floor for his output.

items.h: Derrick Henry s Surprising Bust in Week 6 Loss
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry was held to a season-low 17 carries for just 58 yards and a costly fourth-quarter fumble in an upset loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The superstar back was expected to carry an extra-heavy workload with Lamar Jackson (ankle) sidelined and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley under center. Expectations were also high because the Browns had just allowed 116 rushing yards and a touchdown on 24 carries to Jets backup running back Braelon Allen the previous week. Baltimore's offensive line struggled beyond blocking for Henry, allowing Huntley to be sacked three times. Henry's late fumble that led to Cleveland's comeback punctuated his bust…

items.h: Derrick Henry Primed for Another Heavy Workload in Week 6
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry and the Ravens offense will once again look to backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to take the helm against the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 as Lamar Jackson (ankle) was ruled out Friday afternoon. Henry's role with Huntley at quarterback remained largely unchanged as he logged 24 rushing attempts in Week 5, in keeping with his 23-rush average this season. However, seven of those rushes came in overtime, and Henry carried the ball just five times in the second half. Admittedly, the Ravens had only nine minutes of possession in that half, which almost certainly limited Henry's opportunities. For the season, roughly 40% of the team's total targets and…

items.h: Derrick Henry eclipses 100 yards, catches TD in Week 5
items.s: Derrick Henry rushed for 102 yards on 24 carries, adding an 18-yard touchdown reception in Sunday's 30-23 OT win over the Falcons. Henry picked up 32 of his rushing yards in the Ravens' one overtime possession, but he nevertheless recorded his highest yardage total since Week 1. This was the first time in five games in which Henry did not find the end zone on the ground, but he did come up with his first TD reception of the season. Even in his 11th NFL season, Henry remains among the best running backs in the league.

items.h: Derrick Henry Tops 100 Rushing Yards, Scores Through Air in Week 5
items.s: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry delivered another strong fantasy performance Sunday night, rushing 24 times for 102 yards and catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in a 30-23 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. Henry faced a defense that entered the game allowing an NFL-best 48.3 rushing yards per contest, but Baltimore continued feeding him the ball with Lamar Jackson (ankle) sidelined. His touchdown came on a third-quarter screen from Tyler Huntley, marking his first receiving score since October 2024. Henry later took a direct snap for the game-tying two-point conversion with 40 seconds remaining in regulation. He wasn't finished, either. The veteran…

items.h: Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards while catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
items.s: Henry unsurprisingly worked as the focal point of Baltimore's offense in the absence of Lamar Jackson (ankle). The star running back pulled the Ravens within two points with his 18-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Baltimore's two-point conversion attempt after that touchdown failed, but Henry took matters into his own hands to convert a game-tying two-point conversion out of the wildcat formation with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He then tacked on 32 rushing yards on Baltimore's touchdown drive in OT to top the century mark on the ground for the first time since Week 1.…

items.h: Henry carried the ball 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans. He also caught both his targets for six yards.
items.s: The star RB found the end zone for a fourth straight game to begin the season, rumbling in for a five-yard score on the Ravens' first possession. Henry already has seven rushing TDs, putting him firmly on pace for his ninth straight season in double digits, to go along with 374 rushing yards on 4.2 yards per carry. He'll look to extend his TD streak in in a Week 5 road trip to Atlanta.

items.h: Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Henry scored a four-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter and a three-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, but he was denied the hat trick in the fourth quarter, when a would-be third rushing score was ruled down at the 1-yard line on replay, and Henry's subsequent effort to get in on fourth down was stuffed. The 32-year-old Henry is showing no signs of slowing down, as he has six touchdowns through three games and is averaging just over 100 rushing yards per game heading into a Week 4 home game against the winless Titans.

items.h: Henry carried the ball 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
items.s: The five-time Pro Bowler punched it in from one yard out on a wildcat snap late in the first quarter to open the scoring. Henry wasn't able to break any big gains, however, with his longest run going for just eight yards. He's made four trips to the end zone in two games to begin the season, piling up 214 rushing yards and 38 receiving yards as well, and Henry will look to keep rolling in a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

items.h: Week 1 winners and losers: Caleb Williams and Josh Allen dominate; Ja'Marr Chase disappoints
items.s: Caleb Williams, Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 1, while Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London and Colston Loveland had very quiet days.

items.h: Henry rushed 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns and brought in his only target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.s: Much like he'd done at the expense of the Bills in Week 1 of last season, Henry turned in one of his signature performances right out of the gate, and he struck for his first two touchdowns in the first half from four and 32 yards away. The superstar running back added a three-yard scoring run early in the fourth quarter, and he consistently ripped off chunk gains throughout the afternoon at the expense of an overwhelmed Colts front. Henry's workload won't change under new head coach Jesse Minter if Sunday is any indication, and the perennial Pro Bowl back carries a stellar outlook for a…

items.h: Henry will head into the Ravens' Week 1 game against the Colts with Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali as his backup options, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Though Keaton Mitchell is now with the Chargers after the Ravens non-tendered him back in the spring, Henry will be supported by a pair of familiar sidekicks. Ali is expected to serve as the Ravens' primary kickoff returner and will see most of his snaps on special teams, while Hill returns to his usual role as the top change-of-pace option. Rookie fifth-round pick Adam Randall (undisclosed) could also factor into the equation at some point this season, though not until at least Week 5 after the Ravens placed him on injured reserve. The makeup of the backfield once again points to the…

items.h: Henry is expected to get his normal workload this season but will also be more involved in the passing game, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Henry has logged 280-plus carries in six of his last seven seasons, with the exception being 2021 with the Titans when he was limited to 219 carries in eight regular-season games due to a foot injury. He's routinely seen some of the highest usage among running backs the last few years, and that trend doesn't look like it's going to change in 2026 under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who oversaw Chicago's third-ranked rushing attack last year. The play calling for Henry may look different, however -- the veteran running back has seen more designed runs to the perimeter in training…
